summary: Scoped submission and score-write fixes passed 42 emulator tests and were deployed to hackathon-tokyo on 2026-10-18 (Asia/Tokyo) using contact@cognisorai.com. The live release was read back and matched the tested rules exactly. This is not an overall security approval: existing authentication and event-isolation risks remain and require a separate migration. No production records or judge marks were modified.

findings.check: Automatic host workflow and ownership continuity
findings.issue: Fixed in the repository, with ownership rules now deployed: admin-assisted publishing could lock the original host out of republishing, legacy linked listings could fail on missing creator metadata, and republishing reset the judging rubric.
findings.recommendation: Keep the ownership-preserving publishing change and seed-once rubric logic. Full host, participant, invite/approval and judging workflows are tested with arbitrary new event IDs; retain approval, deadline and pause/close restrictions.

findings.issue: Fixed and deployed: the ElevenLabs document omits submissionMode and the previous direct field read denied legitimate submissions. A teammate array query also failed when evaluating an unrelated missing owner field.
findings.recommendation: Retain the emulator regressions for participant and teammate queries and writes, including imported deadlines, closed events and explicit organiser reopening.

findings.issue: Fixed and deployed: participants could inject preliminary marks, and approved staff could overwrite another judge's maps or project content.
findings.recommendation: Keep score fields organiser/judge-controlled and enforce per-UID map diffs, with separate final-round shortlist validation.

findings.issue: Existing code trusts a portal-admin email pattern without requiring verified email or an admin custom claim. This bootstrap was not changed during the submission patch.
findings.recommendation: Migrate the existing internal administrator to a server-managed identity/claim before removing the bootstrap; do not lock out the organiser with an unplanned role change.

findings.issue: Existing approved staff/host reads are broad, staff event assignments can be self-edited, and invite/membership authority needs a coordinated review. The patch protects judge-owned map entries, not event-level authorization.
findings.recommendation: Move event assignments under organiser authority and validate invite/membership bindings before enforcing matching event-scoped queries.

findings.issue: New score-map writes have score, note-length and criteria-map bounds, but dynamic criterion values/totals need server-side validation. Submission owners still read the existing mixed submission/marks document.
findings.recommendation: Validate each criterion and computed total against organiser criteria in a trusted service, and separate private judging notes if they must be hidden from participants.
